summary: npm package ships only an obfuscated phishing-style HTML page (fake Cloudflare Turnstile)
details: Package contains a single file index.html with a fake 'Just a moment...' Cloudflare Turnstile interstitial and heavily obfuscated bottom-of-file JavaScript (hex-encoded identifiers of the form _0x...., with a destination URL reconstructed at runtime from concatenated string fragments including 'cloudf'). package.json declares main=index.html, files=[index.html], and no scripts or lifecycle hooks. The HTML is not loaded by npm install or by require()/import of the package, so installing or consuming this package does not execute the obfuscated page against the installer. The package has no library functionality; its only shipped content is a phishing-style landing page (the package name suggests a Cathay Pacific ticket lure), consistent with the npm registry being used as hosting/CDN for phishing content rather than as a code supply-chain vector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
